rules.when: The task is SUBSTANTIAL design work: building or redesigning a real UI, product surface, or visual system; a major architecture or system-shape decision; or the final taste convergence on a UI actively being built. Substantial means the outcome is a design that people will live with, not a tweak. This rule does NOT cover routine framing, small artifact edits, or 'how do I change this Lavish/Paper document' work.
rules.why: Captain 2026-09-09: Fable is RESERVED for substantial design work only - real UI building and redesign - because the weekly Fable model window is the scarcest resource in the fleet. Opus is the fallback when Fable is tight or exhausted; never let a Fable-tight window silently downgrade a genuine design task below strong-reasoning class (AGENTS.md section 4).

rules.when: The task is ordinary judgment work that is NOT substantial UI/redesign building: architecture questions with a known shape, API boundaries, tradeoff analysis, product framing, clarifying questions to the captain, planning and Lavish/Paper plan iteration, critiquing an artifact, or an edit to an existing document or board WHERE THE EDIT ITSELF NEEDS JUDGMENT - deciding what the artifact should say, restructuring it, or choosing among variants. An already-decided mechanical or bulk artifact edit is NOT this rule - that is the speed-class fan-out rule below. A targeted typo, one-file fix, or rote rename is NEVER this rule either - it is the trivial-mechanical rule, even when the file is a document.
rules.why: Captain 2026-09-09: Opus is the standing Claude model for judgment, orchestration, and everything short of substantial design. Do not spend the Fable window here - explicitly not on Lavish/Paper document edits or routine framing. The Opus-versus-Cursor line on artifact edits is the captain's own standing Explore policy: Cursor takes already-decided mechanical edits and rough-variant fan-out so Claude quota stays on judgment; Opus takes the edit when the content is the open question rather than the typing. This rule is consulted only when work is being DELEGATED, so it deliberately carries no in-session or do-it-inline carve-outs: those govern whether to delegate at all and live in the Explore prose of docs/routing-policy.md. Keeping them out is what stops a speed-class typo from matching here and landing on Opus.

rules.when: The task is frontend taste, layout, or visual convergence work on an existing surface: polish visual hierarchy, spacing, or brand feel; converge a surface on its final look. Not a bulk fan-out of rough options to compare (that is the speed-class rule below), and not a full redesign (that is rule 1).
rules.why: Captain 2026-09-09, answering firstmate's proposal directly - his words: "Move taste polish back to Fable - I want Fable's eye on all visual convergence, not just redesigns." Firstmate had moved this class to Opus to conserve the Fable window and flagged it for his veto; he vetoed it. So ALL visual convergence is Fable work, not only substantial redesign, and this rule must never fall to a speed-class model: Opus is the only fallback when Fable is tight, and a tight Fable window still never demotes visual convergence below strong-reasoning class. Generating rough variants to compare remains speed-class below - that is producing options, not converging on one.

rules.when: The task is exploratory UI or Paper fan-out, or an already-decided mechanical artifact edit: generate several rough variants or surfaces quickly so the captain can compare, or apply a settled bulk edit to Lavish/Paper HTML. Fast and low-ambiguity, where quality-good-enough beats frontier reasoning. Not a final taste pass, and not an edit whose content is still an open question (that is the ordinary-judgment rule above).
rules.why: Speed-class fan-out and mechanical artifact work, per the captain's standing Explore policy - keeps Claude quota on judgment. Cursor first (no effort flag on Cursor); Codex next. Convergence on the winner may escalate to rule 1 if it becomes substantial design.

rules.when: The task is a chore: docs, CI hygiene, Linear hygiene, renames, formatting, dependency bumps, or other low-ambiguity housekeeping.
rules.why: Fastest cheap path. Cursor first; Codex fallback.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit: targeted typo, one-file fix, rote rename, or similarly narrow low-ambiguity coding.

The task is agent-driven computer use: operating a web console or browser UI to configure a service, provision or rotate an access key, set up a vendor dashboard, or similar browser-heavy operations that do not require the captain's own identity or billing authority.
rules.why: Captain 2026-09-08 (upgrading his 2026-09-07 note): GPT-6 (codex) is SUBSTANTIALLY better than Fable for computer use - codex is the only routine lane for it. When the codex lane is out of credits, PARK the task until the credits reset rather than falling back to another model (captain parked the live Plain pass on exactly this call); another harness only on a current explicit captain instruction. Owner-identity and billing steps still go to the captain per charter.

rules.when: The task is adversarial review, no-mistakes review, or a second-opinion pass on code another model authored.
rules.why: Prefer a different family than the author. Codex is the standing review default; Claude-as-Opus only if Codex is tight. Review is never Fable work.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature or risky refactor where architecture is already decided and the work is primarily implementation with remaining technical ambiguity.
rules.why: Codex is the mid/frontier implementer (smarter than pure speed, faster than a Claude judgment model). Cursor second. Claude-as-Opus last to conserve the Claude account window.

rules.when: The task is an ordinary ship: feature slice, bug fix, or refactor with clear acceptance criteria and limited ambiguity.
rules.why: Default implementation path. Cursor for speed; Codex when Cursor headroom is tight or the slice needs more frontier punch.
